patterns_data.pattern_details: The largest issue is not a clear utilization or reimbursement trend but a validation problem. These signals should be treated as data and classification issues first, because business action on utilization management or provider economics could be misdirected until the mapping is confirmed.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If authorization and facility mapping are wrong, policy, network, and UM actions will target the wrong problem.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM, reimbursement, and data-quality audit of authorization-to-claim mapping and facility crosswalks in GA and PA for the listed inpatient DRGs before changing policy, provider strategy, or denial rules.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase is explicitly flagged as an authorization or mapping shift and includes unmapped facility values, so the data must be validated before business action.

GA PPO Local claims in the Not Mapped facility bucket add about $213K, led by about $89K in metabolic disorders and about $80K in hip/femur cases.
PA PPO Local claims in the Not Mapped facility bucket add about $113K, including about $79K at ATLANTICARE REGIONAL MEDICAL CTR and about $34K in sepsis cases.

patterns_data.pattern_details: A meaningful share of remaining spend is driven by rare, high-cost inpatient cases across multiple providers rather than recurring volume. Most of these signals come from one to three admissions at a time, often with very high paid per admit and unusual clinical presentations. These cases should be handled through case-level review and payment validation, not broad utilization or network policy changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Low-count outliers can materially distort trend results and need a different response than recurring admission growth.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Open case-level reviews for the named providers and DRGs to confirm clinical severity, coding accuracy, and payment integrity, then separate true catastrophic cases from actionable recurring patterns.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Most of the impact comes from one- to three-admission spikes with low baseline counts, so case legitimacy and payment accuracy should be confirmed before broader action.
evidence_summary: MARY WASHINGTON HOSPITAL INC in VA shows multiple single-case spikes, including cardiac valve replacement at about $35K and an unrelated major O.R. procedure at about $35K.
DCH REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER in GA has rare infection and surgical outliers, including candidal sepsis at about $38K and a dialysis catheter complication surgery at about $29K.
MERCY HEALTH - ST. JOSEPH WARREN HOSPITAL in OH and MARY WASHINGTON HOSPITAL INC in VA also show rare sepsis and heart failure outliers ranging from about $14K to $29K per case.
These groups are dominated by one to three admissions each.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Several smaller operational spikes are concentrated in individual providers or sites with low starting volumes. The largest is MARY WASHINGTON HOSPITAL INC in VA, while ME CRITICAL ACCESS and MO Medicare HMO show small but high-cost inpatient episodes. These look more like emerging provider mix changes or isolated site-level events than broad product-wide trends.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Low-baseline provider shifts can grow quickly and are best addressed early with targeted provider and site management.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have network and UM teams confirm whether these are sustained referral or site-of-care changes; if sustained, set provider-specific action plans, and if isolated, exclude them from broader policy conclusions.
patterns_data.validation_reason: These patterns are flagged as low baseline or low volume, so they need confirmation before being treated as durable trends.
